project.title: The Next Page
project.description: On the morning a neighborhood bookbindery is due to close, a granddaughter discovers that her grandfather's craft still has a place in contemporary Addis Ababa.

creative_direction.visual_style: Observational contemporary Addis Ababa urban drama, intimate performances, natural dawn and sunset light, tactile paper and thread, grounded production design, authentic Ethiopian handwoven cotton textiles used naturally in contemporary clothing; varied neighborhood wardrobes, not costume uniformity
creative_direction.music_style: Original restrained instrumental with a warm plucked-string motif and soft hand percussion; no sampled recordings or imitation of a specific ceremonial form

characters.description: Hana, a fictional Ethiopian woman in her early twenties, observant and practical. Wardrobe continuity: a contemporary white cotton habesha kemis with restrained handwoven tibeb bands at the hem and sleeves, plus a lightweight netela shawl worn naturally while working. Keep the woven cotton texture visible, her appearance consistent and natural, and avoid glamorized stereotypes; no real-person likeness.

Bekele, a fictional Ethiopian man in his late sixties, Hana's grandfather and a patient neighborhood bookbinder. Wardrobe continuity: a simple white cotton shirt with a soft handwoven gabi draped over his shoulders, showing subtle woven texture and border. Gentle presence, expressive hands, no real-person likeness.

Sami, a fictional Ethiopian boy about twelve, a neighbor who brings a battered school notebook to be repaired. Contemporary school clothes with a small, understated handwoven cotton scarf; age-appropriate and practical, no real-person likeness.
